newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet following this week's active sales, which "cleaned-up" most showlists, feedlot sources said.
Sales Wednesday at $69.00 per cwt, were up $3.00 from last week's top price.
Fed cattle next week were seen steady to $1.00 higher amid continued strong beef prices and tight supplies of finished cattle, sources said.
Showlists for next week were seen smaller and holding a large percentage of 'green' or unfinished animals, they said.
About 110,500 head of cattle were confirmed sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area for the week to date, far exceeding this week's estimated showlist of 85,000.
Kansas sales this week were pegged at 79,700 head, which also were larger than the week's estimated showlist of 69,000.
The tight supplies of finished cattle contributed to the strength in beef values, cattle feeders said.

Beef prices Wednesday jumped $1.97 to $2.21 per cwt higher on 261 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavy weight choice beef was quoted up $2.21 at $104.62, an advance of $8.11 in the last week, USDA statistics showed.
